name: Multilevel Monte Carlo: the MLMC complexity theorem (Giles 2015, Theorem 1)

milestones.title: §1.1 — variance of a Monte Carlo average
milestones.description: For $N$ independent samples $X_1,\dots,X_N$ with common variance $v$, the Monte Carlo average $N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^N X_n$ has variance $N^{-1}v$ (Giles 2015, §1.1: \"The variance of this estimate is $N^{-1}\mathbb{V}[P]$\").

milestones.title: Eq. (2.1) — mean square error = variance + squared bias
milestones.description: If $Y$ is an approximation to $\mathbb{E}[P]$, then the mean square error is $\mathrm{MSE} \equiv \mathbb{E}\big[(Y-\mathbb{E}[P])^2\big] = \mathbb{V}[Y] + \big(\mathbb{E}[Y]-\mathbb{E}[P]\big)^2$ (Giles 2015, §2.1, eq. (2.1)).

milestones.title: Eq. (2.3) — the multilevel estimator has mean $\mathbb{E}[P_L]$
milestones.description: If $Y=\sum_{\ell=0}^L Y_\ell$ with $\mathbb{E}[Y_0]=\mathbb{E}[P_0]$ and $\mathbb{E}[Y_\ell]=\mathbb{E}[P_\ell-P_{\ell-1}]$ for $\ell\ge1$, then $\mathbb{E}[Y]=\mathbb{E}[P_L]$ (Giles 2015, §2.1, eq. (2.3); the telescoping identity of §1.3).

milestones.title: Eq. (2.3) — variances of independent level estimators add
milestones.description: If the level estimators $Y_0,\dots,Y_L$ are independent, then $\mathbb{V}\big[\sum_{\ell=0}^L Y_\ell\big]=\sum_{\ell=0}^L \mathbb{V}[Y_\ell]$; with $\mathbb{V}[Y_\ell]=N_\ell^{-1}V_\ell$ this is $\mathbb{V}[Y]=\sum_{\ell=0}^L N_\ell^{-1}V_\ell$ (Giles 2015, §2.1, eq. (2.3)).

milestones.title: Eq. (1.1) — the optimal cost for a given variance
milestones.description: For per-sample variances $V_\ell>0$ and costs $C_\ell>0$ and a variance target $\tau>0$ (the paper's $\varepsilon^2$), the least total cost $\sum_\ell N_\ell C_\ell$ over real $N_\ell>0$ with $\sum_\ell N_\ell^{-1}V_\ell\le\tau$ is $\tau^{-1}\big(\sum_\ell\sqrt{V_\ell C_\ell}\big)^2$, attained at $N_\ell=\mu\sqrt{V_\ell/C_\ell}$ with $\mu=\tau^{-1}\sum_\ell\sqrt{V_\ell C_\ell}$ (Giles 2015, §1.3, eq. (1.1)).

milestones.title: Eq. (2.2) — Theorem 1 for the standard multilevel estimator
milestones.description: The conclusion of Theorem 1 holds for the estimator (2.2), $Y_\ell=N_\ell^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^{N_\ell}\big(P_\ell^{(\ell,n)}-P_{\ell-1}^{(\ell,n)}\big)$ with $P_{-1}\equiv0$, built from independent samples $\omega^{(\ell,n)}$, under conditions (i), (iii), (iv) with $V_\ell\equiv\mathbb{V}[P_\ell-P_{\ell-1}]$ and the expected per-sample cost $C_\ell$ (Giles 2015, §2.1, eq. (2.2)–(2.3) and Theorem 1).
